# 毘尼母經

**ID:** T1463
**Volume:** T24
**Category:** 律部類
**Original Category:** 律部
**Byline:** 失譯
**Date:** 350–431
**Juans:** 8
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1463

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

An eight-fascicle anonymous Chinese rendering of the **Vinaya-mātṛkā** — a systematic index/synopsis of Vinaya rule-categories, parallel to the Sarvāstivāda *Vinaya-mātṛkā* ([KR6k0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0022)) but reflecting a different school tradition (probably **Dharmaguptaka** or **Haimavata**, on the basis of the doctrinal positions cited). 毘尼 *pínì* transliterates *vinaya*; 母 *mǔ* "mother" translates *mātṛkā*. Translator and date unknown; the catalog tradition assigns it to "lost translation" (失譯), with a probable date of late-Eastern Jìn / early-Liú-Sòng (4th–5th c.).

**Abstract**

The *Pínì-mǔ jīng* is one of the most important Indian *vinaya*-exegetical works preserved in Chinese, second only to the *Sàpóduō pínì pípóshā* ([KR6k0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0021)) in scope. The eight fascicles systematically expound rule-categories (the doctrinal taxonomy of *prātimokṣa* offences, the procedural taxonomy of *karmavācanā*-types, the institutional taxonomy of *saṅgha*-types, etc.). The school identification has been debated: doctrinal evidence has been variously read to suggest Dharmaguptaka, Haimavata, or even Mahāsāṃghika affinity. Modern scholarship (Hirakawa 1960, Clarke 2004) treats it as an indispensable witness for Indian *vinaya*-scholasticism predating the Mūlasarvāstivāda recensions.
